questions.prompt: In tool use, what does the model do?

options.text: It runs the tool code inside itself, then returns only the result.
options.explanation: Google's docs say the model does not execute the function itself.

options.text: It asks for a tool call. Your app or the vendor runs it.
options.explanation: Right. Google: the model does not execute the function itself.

questions.prompt: A tool is described only as "Does image stuff". What is the risk?

options.text: None. The model reads the code behind the tool and learns what it does.
options.explanation: The model sees the name, description and input shape you give it. It does not see your code.

options.text: The tool will cost more tokens, because vague words are longer to read.
options.explanation: A short description costs fewer tokens. The risk is about wrong or missed calls.

options.text: The model may pick it at the wrong time, or never. Names guide the choice.
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic says Claude decides based on the request and the tool's description. Google says to be clear and specific.

options.text: Your app always runs every tool, including the vendor's built-in tools.
options.explanation: Anthropic says server tools run on Anthropic's infrastructure, and OpenAI has built-in tools. Only client tools run in your app.

options.text: The model runs every tool itself, so no app or vendor code is ever needed.
options.explanation: Google says the model does not execute the function itself.

options.text: The vendor runs built-in or server tools. Your app runs your own tools.
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic: client tools run in your application, server tools run on Anthropic's infrastructure. OpenAI also has built-in tools.
